# Assignment answers

## Question 1


```{r}
#converting intuit into factors
intuit <- intuit %>%
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),
    state = factor(state),
    zip = factor(zip),
    version2013 = factor(version2013),
    upgraded = factor(upgraded),
    payroll = factor(payroll),
    bizflag = factor(bizflag),
    sex = factor(sex),
    res = factor(res),
    training = factor(training)
  )

intuit.wave2 <- intuit.wave2 %>%
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),
    state = factor(state),
    zip = factor(zip),
    version2013 = factor(version2013),
    upgraded = factor(upgraded),
    payroll = factor(payroll),
    bizflag = factor(bizflag),
    sex = factor(sex)
    
  )

```

## Question 2



```{r}
# Split into train/test based on 'training' variable
intuit.train <- intuit %>% filter(training == 1)
intuit.test <- intuit %>% filter(training == 0)
```


```{r}
# Build Logistic Regression Model
model_lr <- glm(res ~ version2013 + upgraded + payroll + bizflag + sex + last + numords + dollars + sincepurch + speeddown + speedup + income + medhvalue,
                family = "binomial", data = intuit.train)
print(model_lr)

# Build Neural Network Model
model_nn <-nnet(res ~ version2013 + upgraded + payroll + bizflag + sex + last + numords + dollars + sincepurch + speeddown + speedup + income + medhvalue,size=5,decay=0.1,maxit=1000,data=intuit.train)
print(model_nn)



#Modelling logistic regression enhanced
model_lr_new <- glm(res ~ version2013 + upgraded + payroll + bizflag + sex +income+medhvalue+
                      
                    dollars+numords+ sincepurch+last +speeddown+speedup+ I(income^2) +
                      I(medhvalue^2) + I(sincepurch^2) +
                      
                      I(speeddown^2) +
                      I(speedup^2) +
                      I(last^2) +I(log(income))+
                     I(log(numords))+
                      I(log(dollars))+
                      payroll:upgraded +
                      bizflag:income+
        payroll:bizflag +
        sincepurch:upgraded,
                      
                      family = "binomial", data = intuit.train)
print(model_lr_new)


```
```{r}
# Make Predictions for training sample and test sample

intuit.train <- intuit.train %>%
  mutate(pred_lr = predict(model_lr, type = "response"),
         pred_nn = predict(model_nn, type = "raw")[,1],
         pred_lr_new = predict(model_lr_new, type = "response"))

intuit.test <- intuit.test %>%
  mutate(pred_lr = predict(model_lr, newdata = intuit.test, type = "response"),
         pred_nn = predict(model_nn, newdata = intuit.test, type = "raw")[,1],
          pred_lr_new = predict(model_lr_new,newdata=intuit.test,type = "response"))

```


```{r}
#Model performance comparison for training data set
# Gains Plot: Training Sample
gainsplot(intuit.train$pred_lr, intuit.train$pred_nn, intuit.train$pred_lr_new,label.var = intuit.train$res)



```


```{r}
# Model performance comparison for test data set
# Gains Plot: Test Sample

gainsplot(intuit.test$pred_lr, intuit.test$pred_nn,intuit.test$pred_lr_new, label.var = intuit.test$res)
```


```{r}
# VARIABLE IMPORTANCE PLOTS

# For LOGISTIC REGRESSION training set

varimpplot(model_lr, target = "res", data = intuit.train)


```
```{r}
# For logistic regression test set

varimpplot(model_lr, target = "res", data = intuit.test)
```
```{r}
# For NEURAL NETWORK training set
varimpplot(model_nn, target = "res", data = intuit.train)

```


```{r}
# For NEURAL NETWORK test set
varimpplot(model_nn, target = "res", data = intuit.test)

```
```{r}
# Scoring intuit.wave2 using model_lr_new

intuit.wave2$best.score_log <- predict(model_lr_new, newdata = intuit.wave2, type = "response")






```


```{r}
# Scoring intuit.wave2 using model_nn

intuit.wave2$best.score_nn <- predict(model_nn, newdata = intuit.wave2, type = "raw")[,1]

```


```{r}
# Expected Profit Calculation for logistic regression based model
library(dplyr)
profit_per_conversion <- 180     # Lifetime net profit
mail_cost <- 1.60                # Mailing cost
opportunity_cost <- 5.60         # Benchmark to beat

# Calculate expected profit for each customer
intuit.wave2_logprofit<- intuit.wave2 %>% 
  mutate(
    expected_profit_log = profit_per_conversion * best.score_log - mail_cost,
    target.wave2_log = ifelse(expected_profit_log >= opportunity_cost, 1, 0)
  )
print(sum(intuit.wave2_logprofit$expected_profit_log[intuit.wave2_logprofit$target.wave2_log == 1]))
print(sum(intuit.wave2_logprofit$target.wave2_log==1))

#Logistic model: 8,118 customers targeted, expected profit $125,577
#That is $15.47 per targeted customer, or $9.87 above the $5.60 opportunity cost

```

```{r}
# Expected Profit Calculation for Neural Network based model
library(dplyr)
profit_per_conversion <- 180     # Lifetime net profit
mail_cost <- 1.60                # Mailing cost
opportunity_cost <- 5.60         # Benchmark to beat

# Calculate expected profit for each customer
intuit.wave2_nnprofit<- intuit.wave2 %>% 
  mutate(
    expected_profit_nn = profit_per_conversion * best.score_nn - mail_cost,
    target.wave2_nn = ifelse(expected_profit_nn >= opportunity_cost, 1, 0)
  )
print(sum(intuit.wave2_nnprofit$expected_profit_nn[intuit.wave2_nnprofit$target.wave2_nn == 1]))
print(sum(intuit.wave2_nnprofit$target.wave2_nn==1))
#Neural network: 8,201 customers targeted, expected profit $131,407
#That is $16.02 per targeted customer, or $10.42 above the $5.60 opportunity cost

```
